title: Week four of creating a game called Wobbly Blocks with Claude Fable, ChatGPT and Three.js.
author: BadgerTom
selftext:
This is Wobbly Blocks, a physics stacking game I’ve been building using Claude Fable/Opus 5.5, with ChatGPT Astra for image and texture generation. It runs straight in the browser with Three.js. I also used Suno and ElevenLabs for music and voices. Works great on desktops and touchscreen mobile devices.

Simple idea: stack blocks, keep your balance, and see how far you can push questionable structural decisions. The blocks have little faces, different shapes and materials (almost 200 variations you can collecf), and a variety of worlds to build in (and little voices when they fall ... ahhhh!).

It took a lot of iteration to be a complete game with mechanics and difficulty accommodations, but it was a functional game initially in about 15 minutes!

The video shows where it’s at now. I’d love some honest feedback: does the stacking look satisfying? Anything about the visuals or movement that feels off?

Also interested in how others here are handling the gap between a nice AI-generated asset and something that actually works in-game. I have started using meshy and blender for another game. This one is just about done.

[wobblyblocks.com](https://wobblyblocks.com)
